title: Projective Hom scalar comparison represents the canonical unit transpose
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $F=S\otimes_R-$ on modules and termwise on cochain complexes, $U$ restriction of scalars, $Q_R,Q_S$ the derived localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $LF=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Identify ordinary modules with the one-object bottom-topology module-sheaf categories [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison]. Let $P$ be any bounded-above complex of projective $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] and $N$ any $R$-complex. Use the product Hom complexes [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], equivalently [def-pur-hom-complex], and their canonical projective-source model comparisons with derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let
$$\chi:F\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,N)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(FP,FN)$$
be the normalized chain map of [lem-pc-normalized-ring-hom-extension], specified by $(\chi(s\otimes f))_p(t\otimes x)=st\otimes f_p(x)$ for every homogeneous family $f$.

For arbitrary $E,L\in D(R)$ let $\beta_{E,L}:LF(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L))\to R\operatorname{Hom}_S(LFE,LFL)$ be the scalar-adjunction transpose of $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,\eta_L)$ followed by the inverse of the evaluation-normalized internal-Hom scalar adjunction [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction], where $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to ULF$ is the unit of $LF\dashv U$. Under the canonical flat scalar-extension and projective-Hom model comparisons, $Q_S\chi$ equals $\beta_{Q_RP,Q_RN}$ in $D(S)$. Its internal-Hom scalar adjunction is represented by the chain isomorphism
$$U\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(FP,FN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,U(FN)),\qquad g_p\longmapsto(x\mapsto g_p(1\otimes x)),$$
with inverse $h_p\mapsto(t\otimes x\mapsto t h_p(x))$. In these models Hom applied to $\eta_N$ is $f_p\mapsto(x\mapsto1\otimes f_p(x))$, and its scalar adjoint is exactly $s\otimes f_p\mapsto(t\otimes x\mapsto st\otimes f_p(x))$. The family $\beta$ is natural in arbitrary derived morphisms of $E,L$, including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms; the displayed equality respects changes of projective representatives and arbitrary target quasi-isomorphisms. No finite-generation, perfectness, or boundedness hypothesis on $N$ is imposed, and no invertibility of $\chi$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0E1W (lemma-upgrade-adjoint-tensor-RHom), proof, and Equation 0E1X (equation-base-change-RHom): projective-source chain representative and unit normalization.

proof.text: Work in ordinary modules using [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison]; tensor symmetry identifies the right-tensor convention with $F=S\otimes_R-$ and sends $x\otimes1$ to $1\otimes x$. Put $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,N)$, $J=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(FP,FN)$, and $T=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,U(FN))$. By [lem-trf-flat-projective-hom-models], $FP$ is bounded above and termwise projective, $F$ preserves every quasi-isomorphism, and there are canonical comparisons $e:Q_RH\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q_RP,Q_RN)$, $c_C:LF(Q_RC)\simeq Q_SFC$, $b:Q_SJ\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_S(LFQ_RP,LFQ_RN)$, and the corresponding comparison for $Q_RT$. The unit and counit in these models are $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ and $s\otimes y\mapsto sy$. These assertions apply to $C=H$ even when $H,N$ are unbounded.

source.place: Tag 0A66 (lemma-RHom-out-of-projective); Tag 0GMT (lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint); Tag 0E1W, choice of models.

proof.text: Define $a:UJ\to T$ in degree $n$ coordinatewise by $a(g)_p(x)=g_p(1\otimes x)$, and define $v:T\to UJ$ by $v(h)_p(t\otimes x)=t h_p(x)$. The latter is balanced since $h_p(rx)=\varphi(r)h_p(x)$, and it is $S$-linear in the input. The equalities $a(v(h))_p(x)=h_p(x)$ and $v(a(g))_p(t\otimes x)=t g_p(1\otimes x)=g_p(t\otimes x)$ prove that these maps are inverse $R$-linear maps on the full products. With the differential of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], evaluation of either $a(dg)$ or $d(a(g))$ at $x\in P^p$ is $d_{FN}g_p(1\otimes x)-(-1)^n g_{p+1}(1\otimes d_Px)$. Thus $a$ is a chain isomorphism (and its inverse is a chain map). This argument uses each product projection separately, with no interchange of tensor and an infinite product.

The localization of $a$ has the evaluation normalization that characterizes the isomorphism $\alpha:U R\operatorname{Hom}_S(LFQ_RP,LFQ_RN)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q_RP,ULFQ_RN)$ in [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction]. Indeed [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model], applied over $R$ to $(P,U(FN))$ and over $S$ to $(FP,FN)$, represents both derived evaluations by their ordinary tensor evaluations. For $x\in P^p$ and $g\in J^n$, evaluation after $a$ is $(-1)^{pn}a(g)_p(x)=(-1)^{pn}g_p(1\otimes x)$. Precomposing the restricted $S$-evaluation by the scalar unit gives the same expression. The restricted evaluation uses the lax tensor map $\lambda:UA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}UB\to U(A\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}B)$ of restriction, the mate $U(\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)\circ U\mu_{UA,UB}\circ\eta$ of the derived scalar tensor comparison $\mu$ of the scalar data [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data] used by [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction]. That data represents $\mu$ on K-flat complexes by the pure-generator chain isomorphism $s\otimes(y\otimes z)\mapsto(s\otimes y)\otimes(1\otimes z)$. Take $A=Q_SFP$, $B=Q_SJ$: $U(FP)$ and $P$ are bounded above with flat $R$-terms, so they are K-flat and tensors with them compute derived tensors. For a K-flat resolution $w:Y\to UJ$, the maps $P\otimes w$, $U(FP)\otimes w$ and $F(U(FP)\otimes w)$ are quasi-isomorphisms ($S$ is flat), so naturality of $\mu$ in $w$ transports its pure-generator formula from $Y$ to $UJ$. With the unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ and counit $s\otimes y\mapsto sy$ of [lem-trf-flat-projective-hom-models], the scalar unit followed by $\lambda$ is therefore represented by the chain map $P\otimes_R UJ\to U(FP\otimes_S J)$ taking $x\otimes g\mapsto1\otimes((1\otimes x)\otimes g)\mapsto(1\otimes(1\otimes x))\otimes(1\otimes g)\mapsto(1\otimes x)\otimes g$. This balanced map has inverse $(t\otimes x)\otimes g\mapsto x\otimes tg$. These inverse maps commute with differentials since $t$ has degree zero; restriction does not change their values. The comparisons of [lem-trf-flat-projective-hom-models] identify this scalar unit with the derived unit and the two Hom models with the indicated derived objects. Thus the displayed equality is an equality of the representing evaluation maps, not just of maps on cohomology. Uniqueness in [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] identifies $Q_Ra$ with $\alpha$ under these comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0E1W, degreewise precomposition by the unit; Tag 0A66 and Tag 0GWQ (remark-internal-hom), evaluation normalization.

proof.text: Under the comparisons of [lem-trf-flat-projective-hom-models], $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q_RP,\eta_{Q_RN})$ is represented by $k:H\to T$, $k(f)_p(x)=1\otimes f_p(x)$: apply the target map $\eta_N$ in each product coordinate. It commutes with the Hom differential because $d_{FN}(1\otimes y)=1\otimes d_Ny$ [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Consequently $\alpha^{-1}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q_RP,\eta_{Q_RN})$ is represented by $vk:H\to UJ$, with $(vk(f))_p(t\otimes x)=t\otimes f_p(x)$.

Take the scalar adjoint of the last map. By [lem-trf-flat-projective-hom-models] the derived scalar adjunction is represented by the ordinary unit and counit. Its adjoint on complexes is therefore $F H\xrightarrow{F(vk)}FUJ\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_J}J$, and on tensors its value is $(s\otimes f)_p(t\otimes x)\mapsto s(t\otimes f_p(x))=st\otimes f_p(x)$. This is exactly the normalization of $\chi$ supplied by [lem-pc-normalized-ring-hom-extension]. Tensor generators in $F H^n$, product projections of $J^n$, and tensor generators in $FP^p$ determine the degree maps, so the chain maps agree. Localizing gives, with the notation of step 1, $\beta_{Q_RP,Q_RN}=b\circ Q_S\chi\circ c_H\circ LF(e^{-1})$, the required equality under the canonical model comparisons.

For arbitrary $E,L$, put $A(E,L)=LF(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L))$ and $B(E,L)=R\operatorname{Hom}_S(LFE,LFL)$. The map $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,\eta_L)$ is natural by bifunctoriality [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and naturality of the adjunction unit. Composing with the natural $\alpha^{-1}$ of [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] and taking the scalar adjoint preserves this naturality: the transpose is $\varepsilon\circ LF(-)$, and both $LF$ and $\varepsilon$ are natural. Hence for any morphism $z$ of $D(R)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(R)$, $B(z)\beta=\beta A(z)$. If $z$ is invertible, multiplying this square by $A(z)^{-1}$ and $B(z)^{-1}$ gives the square for $z^{-1}$. The canonical model comparisons in [lem-trf-flat-projective-hom-models] commute with localization, so the equality of step 5 respects changes of projective representatives and arbitrary target quasi-isomorphisms, including their inverses. No boundedness or finiteness of $N$ was used, and equality of these morphisms asserts no invertibility of $\chi$.
